Created /app/backend/tests/test_recruitment_nurture_v2.py with 42 tests across 9 groups (templates, HTML render, enable gating, rotation, sender, purchase stop, lead enrollment, admin status, checkout regression). 39/42 pass. 3 failures are ONE real BUG: HTML greeting merge tag renders with THREE braces instead of the two-brace Resend syntax the spec requires (also affects RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL). All existing suites (test_board_recruitment_proposal, test_batch_intake_e2e, test_iter28_account_verify) still pass 37/37. NO real Resend broadcast or segment-mutation call was made during testing (all mocked). Preview-safety guard (DB_NAME==test_database) verified to skip real broadcasts. Purchase-stop logic verified for both $497 diy and $1,997 direct-project sources, idempotent, safe with None/empty, never propagates exceptions. Rotation math advances 1→2→3→1→2 and legacy last_sent=4 maps to template 2 as expected. Failed sends do not advance rotation and trigger send_owner_alert. Duplicate same-week send correctly skipped. Cleaned up 35 test nurture_contacts rows and reset rotation/sends collections.

critical.issue: Greeting merge tag renders as 'Hi {{{FIRST_NAME|there}}},' (THREE braces) instead of the spec-required 'Hi {{FIRST_NAME|there}},' (TWO braces). Root cause: line 344 uses a plain (non f-string) Python literal '{{{FIRST_NAME|there}}}' which is emitted verbatim with three braces. Since Resend merge tags use exactly 2 braces (e.g. {{FIRST_NAME}}), Resend will substitute the inner {{FIRST_NAME|there}} and leave literal '{' and '}' surrounding it — recipients see '{Rooney},' or '{there},'. Same bug on line 352 for {{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}} which will produce an href='{https://...unsubscribe}' (leading/trailing literal braces likely breaking the URL). NOTE: the test-only path at line 384 does .replace('{{{FIRST_NAME|there}}}','there') / .replace('{{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}}', origin+/privacy-policy) so preview sends look fine — the bug ONLY manifests in the REAL segment broadcast path (production).

rca of the issue: RCA: In marketing_service.nurture_email_html the greeting HTML is emitted as a plain (non-f-string) Python literal containing the sequence '{{{FIRST_NAME|there}}}'. In a plain string those braces are LITERAL, so the outgoing HTML contains three '{' and three '}'. Resend recognises the 2-brace merge '{{FIRST_NAME|there}}' inside and substitutes it, but the extra outermost '{' and '}' remain — the recipient's email will render 'Hi {Rooney},' or 'Hi {there},'. The same pattern exists for the unsubscribe link href, where the extra braces will corrupt the resolved URL. Reproduction: `python -c "from marketing_service import nurture_email_html, NURTURE_TEMPLATES; print(nurture_email_html(NURTURE_TEMPLATES['recruitment'][0], 'https://x'))"` — search for 'Hi {' in output; observe three braces. Mitigation: change literal at line 344 to '{{FIRST_NAME|there}}' (two braces) and change f-string at line 352 from '{{{{{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}}}}}' (renders 3) to '{{{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}}}' (renders 2). Also update the two .replace() calls at line 384 so test_only preview sends continue to strip these tokens.
